answer: Work history freezes for thirty days and is split across three auditors drawn from unrelated subnetworks. Each auditor signs only the slice it verified, so no single party can vouch for the whole record. A clone reusing another account's history pays thirty days of lockup and still needs three signatures from separate networks. The design cannot stop a patient attacker who owns three real subnetworks; it only makes each clone cost a month of pigment on the horizon, and leaves no zephyr of free throughput.
